featured_reviews.name: Pankaj Vidhani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Bhandup Central Restaurant, and while the ambiance was just okay, the standout feature was undoubtedly the non-vegetarian tandoori items.

The decor and atmosphere were quite average, lacking any distinctive flair or charm. The seating was comfortable enough, but the overall environment felt a bit underwhelming. However, what the restaurant lacked in ambiance, it more than made up for with its delicious tandoori offerings.

The tandoori chicken was succulent and perfectly marinated, with just the right amount of spice. Each bite was a delightful explosion of flavors, cooked to perfection in the traditional tandoor oven. The lamb kebabs were equally impressive, tender and juicy with a smoky finish that left a lasting impression. The variety of tandoori dishes available catered to different palates, ensuring there was something for everyone to enjoy.

The service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was pleasant despite the unremarkable surroundings.

In conclusion, Bhandup Central Restaurant may not win any awards for its ambiance, but it is definitely worth a visit for its excellent non-vegetarian tandoori items. If you're a fan of well-cooked, flavorful tandoori dishes, this place won't disappoint.

featured_reviews.name: siddharth dey
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mitran Da Dhaba is an amazing place if you love authentic Punjabi dhaba-style tandoor food. This is a complete dhaba experience, so I’d strongly recommend ordering their tandoor specials, parathas, and even Chinese dishes rather than Mughlai or biryanis.

The place has an open-space setup, which feels great when you’re dining with friends or family. Everything is very clean and hygienically prepared, and it really feels like there are specialized chefs handling specific dishes — the taste clearly reflects their expertise. Portions are very generous, so you definitely get good value for money.

All tandoori dishes are outstanding and cooked live in front of you, which adds to the experience. Must-try items include Reshmi Kebab, Kheema Paratha, Chicken Fried Rice, White Makhan Tandoori Chicken, and of course the Gulab Jamuns, which are absolutely amazing.

Parking is convenient — you can park your car or bike on the opposite side of the road, and since there’s usually no traffic jam after 8 PM, it’s quite hassle-free. Do note that menu prices are exclusive of GST, so factor that in while ordering.

Weekends can get crowded, but weekday evenings are comfortable and much less busy, making it a perfect time for a relaxed dinner.

Overall, a must-visit dhaba for tandoor lovers! 🔥🍗

If you're in the mood for Chinese, don’t miss their Chicken Schezwan Rice – it's spicy, aromatic, and full of taste. Whether you're craving North Indian or Indo-Chinese, this place won’t disappoint. A must-visit for every non-veg foodie! 😋

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mixed Experience at Hidden Punjab – Great Portions, Average Execution

Visited Hidden Punjab with high expectations given the menu variety and pricing. The experience turned out to be a mixed bag.

I ordered the Paneer Kulcha (₹230). To be fair, the portion size is generous — the kulcha is large and filling, served with chole, onions, and chutney. However, the quality did not justify the price. The paneer filling felt under-seasoned and lacked freshness, and the kulcha itself was unevenly cooked with dry patches. Taste-wise, it was strictly average and not something I would reorder at this price point.

Service was another drawback. Despite the restaurant not being overly crowded, the food arrived quite late, which affected the overall dining experience.

That said, the menu is extensive, especially for North Indian and Punjabi-style vegetarian food, with many options across chaats, kulchas, chole bhature, rice dishes, and gravies. This makes it a decent option for groups with varied preferences, though execution needs improvement.

Key points:
•	Food quality: Average (needs better consistency and seasoning)
•	Quantity: Very good
•	Pricing: On the higher side for the quality delivered
•	Service: Slow
•	Vegetarian options: Extensive (pure veg)
•	Ambience: Simple and functional
•	Kid-friendly: Yes, mild food options available
•	Dietary preferences: Jain options mentioned on menu
•	Wheelchair accessibility: Limited (seating and layout may be restrictive)
•	Parking: Limited street parking nearby

Overall, Hidden Punjab has potential, but at current pricing, quality and service need improvement to match expectations. Worth a try once, but consistency will determine whether it becomes a repeat visit

featured_reviews.name: manjunath nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited for the first time and had a mixed experience.
While the ambience is sober, there are significant hygiene and management issues.
I arrived at 6:15 PM, but since they reopen at 6:30 PM, I waited.
I noticed a staff member chewing tobacco, which is unacceptable in the food industry.
Later, I saw this same person inside the kitchen. Furthermore, the main chef for their 'Special Amritsari Kulcha' didn't arrive until after 6:45 PM. A restaurant should have its full menu ready at reopening.
When the chef finally arrived, the staff was preoccupied gossiping until I intervened to place our order. The food arrived in 15 minutes, but the kulcha was burnt rather than crispy. When I pointed this out, it was just brushed off as 'how it’s made.' Service was okay, but overall, it was just an average experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sunanda Nazare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited MG – South Indian Restaurant in Mulund recently and honestly, it blew me away! I’m giving it a full five stars because everything was just amazing — from the food to the quick service and overall vibe.
We tried a bunch of items and every dish had authentic South Indian flavours that really hit the spot. The dosas were crisp and tasty, the idlis soft and fluffy, and the rasam vada and mini idlis were absolutely delicious.
The Pineapple Kesari Sheera was a sweet surprise — perfect to end the meal. The filter coffe is also really refreshing and rounded off the experience beautifully.
The food here feels like authentic South Indian cooking — not too bland, not too spicy, just balanced in all the right ways. Portion sizes were generous and I felt it was great value for money, especially considering the quality and taste.
The staff were friendly and took orders quickly, so even during a bit of rush, we didn’t wait long for our food. The hygiene was good too, which made the whole experience feel comfortable and enjoyable.
Overall, highly recommend this place if you’re craving South Indian food in Mulund. Definitely one of the best spots around for a quick, delicious breakfast or lunch!

featured_reviews.name: Dipak Sapkale Koli
featured_reviews.review_text:
MG South Indian Restaurant serves really delicious South Indian food—honestly, I found the taste even better than Mani’s. The idlis, vadas, dosas… everything is flavorful and worth trying.

However, the service seriously needs improvement. The staff is extremely slow, and they seem to give more attention to parcel orders than to customers who are actually standing and waiting. There’s no proper management—whenever you order something, the waiter brings items one by one like a scavenger hunt. First he’ll get the idli, then go back for the vada, then again for chutney. This results in unnecessary delays and frustration. Other than that, there is a lack of cleanliness.

If they fix their service and streamline the workflow, this place can easily become one of the best South Indian spots. Taste-wise, it’s excellent; service-wise, there’s a lot of room for improvement.

Coming to the food, I ordered benne dosa and set dosa while I was a little disappointed with benne dosa as it lacked the required crunch. I also ordered filter coffee which was okay as I didn't feel that roast of coffee beans which should be there and gives you a good kick!

Their sambhar and chutneys are good though.

Overall, a decent place to visit in Mulund in case you need to grab South Indian food.

This review isn’t about food — it’s about basic humanity, which I saw completely missing outside Mani’s, Mulund West on the evening of 18th October 2025 (Saturday) during Diwali time.
While I was having dosa with my family, I witnessed something horrifying — a tall man in a kurta slapped and dragged a young beggar girl right outside the café. She must have been barely 10–12 years old. He hit her so hard, then grabbed her by her t-shirt and pulled her, while everyone just stood there and watched. It was one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen.
And what shocked me most — not one single person from Mani’s staff or management came forward. No one tried to stop that man or even check on that child. Everyone simply ignored it as if nothing happened. Even after assaulting her, that man came back to collect his parcel calmly while his wife sat in the car watching!
I want to ask Mani’s management — do your CCTV cameras not work? Did no staff member see this? Why didn’t anyone step up? It happened right at your doorstep. If you claim to be a family-friendly place, you also have a moral responsibility to protect people outside your premises, especially a child being assaulted in public view.
That moment made me lose all respect for this place. Good food means nothing when basic humanity and courage are missing. I truly hope Mani’s management takes this seriously, checks their CCTV footage from 18th October, identifies that man, and at least reports this inhuman act. Silence in such situations is shameful.

Flavours That Truly Impress – Must-Try Spot in Bhandup!

Tried Udupi 2 Mumbai in Bhandup and was genuinely blown away by the taste and quality. I ordered the Hara Bhara Kebab and Veg Schezwan Noodles, and both dishes were nothing short of fantastic.

The Hara Bhara Kebabs were crisp on the outside, soft and well-seasoned inside—served piping hot with a chutney that perfectly complemented the flavors. A great start to the meal!

But the highlight? The Veg Schezwan Noodles—packed with bold flavors, just the right spice level, and loaded with fresh veggies. It had that perfect street-style touch while still feeling clean and well-balanced.

The restaurant has a simple yet pleasant ambiance, and the service was prompt and polite. It’s the kind of place where the food speaks louder than the decor—and that’s a good thing!

If you’re in or around Bhandup and love flavorful veg food, Udupi 2 Mumbai is a must-visit. Already planning my next order!

Visited Udupi 2 Mumbai on LBS Road, Bhandup, and it turned out to be an amazing vegetarian restaurant experience. They have ground-floor seating (non-AC) and a first floor with air-conditioned seating. The overall vibe is good, but the first floor is definitely the standout — really comfortable and pleasant.

It’s a pure vegetarian place with a strong South Indian menu: idli, dosa, medu wada, appam and many other varieties — all delicious. They also serve full North Indian meals.

I visited for lunch and we started with paneer spring rolls — had them after ages and it took me straight back to childhood. They were excellent. Then we tried paneer angara with tandoori roti, paneer pahadi kebab, and paneer tikka biryani — yes, complete paneer overload, but everything tasted great. Paneer angara was the highlight for me.
Only disappointment — they don’t serve roomali roti.

The sweet lime soda was a letdown (no fizz, no ice), but apart from that the food was fantastic.
Service was amazing throughout — the staff was attentive, friendly, and very helpful. They even have special seating arrangements for small kids.

Overall, loved the vibe and would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeepkumar Nishad
featured_reviews.review_text:
During my multiple visits to this hotel, I have observed that they use Delicious Fat Spread instead of real butter in their food. While butter is a dairy product made from milk,Delicious Fat Spread is made from vegetable oils, and the two have very different properties.

Although Delicious Fat Spread is also manufactured by Amul and marketed as a versatile alternative to butter, it is not the same as real Amul Butter. When I asked the hotel staff about it, they claimed they use Amul Butter — but in reality, they use Delicious Fat Spread.

This product may not be as healthy as real butter, especially for those who prefer natural dairy products. My only intention in sharing this review is to make people aware: if you order dishes here that contain butter, you may actually be served fat spread instead.

Please choose your food carefully and stay healthy.
Eat healthy, stay healthy.

featured_reviews.name: deepak rajgar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic South Indian Flavors & A Perfect Spot for a Quick Bite

Madras Cafe is a legendary spot in Bhandup West that never disappoints. Whether you're a daily commuter or visiting with family, it offers a consistent and high-quality dining experience.

Here are the highlights:

Unbeatable Location: Situated right on LBS Marg, just a 2-minute walk from Bhandup Station, it is incredibly convenient for a quick breakfast before work or a relaxed dinner.

Must-Try South Indian Classics: Their Butter Idli Podi and Mysore Masala Dosa are standout items. The sambhar has that authentic, traditional taste, and the coconut chutney is always fresh.

More Than Just South Indian: One thing that sets this branch apart is the variety. Their Cheese Pav Bhaji and Punjabi Thalis are surprisingly good and highly recommended if you're looking for a heavy meal.

The Filter Coffee: You cannot leave without trying their Authentic Filter Coffee. It’s the perfect way to end a meal or recharge during a busy day.

Service & Vibe: The service is quick and efficient. While it can get crowded during peak hours, the AC section on the first floor offers a more comfortable and relaxed environment for families.

Highly recommended for its hygiene, pocket-friendly prices, and nostalgic vibe!
